ideas.pitch: A game prototype where players can talk to dynamic non-player characters using real-time voice integration, adapting to whatever surprise twist is revealed in Round 2.
ideas.title: VoiceForge NPC
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly mirrors the successful plugin approach that won the Nvidia Hackathon by enabling live conversational mechanics.

ideas.pitch: A 2D atmospheric platformer built with modular game states, ensuring that when Round 2 drops a sudden mechanic shift, the core movement physics can accommodate it seamlessly.
ideas.title: Echoes of Incarnia
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages proven architectural patterns from MLH winning entries while focusing heavily on the round-adaptation constraint.

ideas.pitch: An educational visual novel focused on local water resource management with branching narrative trees designed for rapid script modifications during the final round twist.
ideas.title: AuraQuest Conservation
ideas.why_it_could_win: Builds directly on the narrative structure of past Smart India Hackathon winners, prioritizing educational storytelling and high polish.

ideas.pitch: A mini-game featuring two identical AI agents placed in a prisoner's dilemma scenario, designed to dynamically evolve their cooperative or deceptive strategies live on stage.
ideas.title: Split or Steal Arena
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the algorithmic agent competition strategy that won the Datadog Self-Improving Agents Hack.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight top-down tactical survival prototype where an autonomous agent utilizes open models to make real-time decisions alongside the human player.
ideas.title: DotaBot Arena Prototype
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs heavy technical implementation and AI agent mechanics proven at the OpenAI Open Model Hackathon.
